judged_text: The addMembers action discards the returned promise, renders no pending state, and never clears the usernames input after submission (the diff's own TODO), so the add flow gives no feedback that anything happened. On a slow response the admin sees no change and clicks Add again, re-issuing the identical PUT; and because the reloaded member list is alphabetical, a newly added member whose username sorts beyond the current page never appears in view — the only success signal is the count in 'Group members (N)', so successful adds routinely look like no-ops.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and currently just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without returning/handling the AJAX promise or setting any pending/disabled state. The model method `addMembers` does return a promise and reloads members via `self.findMembers()`, but the controller never clears `usernames` and provides no in-action feedback, making repeated clicks plausible on slow responses. With pagination (`limit/offset` in `group.js` and `findMembers` reloading the current page), a newly added user that sorts beyond the current page will not appear in the reloaded `members` list, so the only visible change may be `user_count`, matching the finding. This is a UX/flow robustness issue rather than a verifiable correctness defect.
